The raw open/prior-close ratio is asymmetric around 1; wrapping it in LN makes it a proper symmetric log-return, a real inner transform rather than an outer wrapper, window and fields unchanged.

Rule 6 flags this exact high-low/dollar_volume-or-open motif as over-mined; window resizes and normalizer crosses were all rejected for archive overlap. The untried lever is the range measure itself: changing the first term from full range to upper-wick (high-close) tests rejection-off-the-high instead of pure range, while the second term and both normalizers stay untouched.

Working memory names RANK($roa) itself as the too-shallow example, a single bare fundamental leaf with no interaction partner. Multiplying by asset_turnover embeds it in a DuPont-style efficiency-adjusted composite, a real second component, no new division/epsilon needed, and only two nodes added.

Same over-mined range/dollar_volume family as rule 6 describes; window and denominator are already known dead ends. Switching the numerator from full range (high-low) to lower-wick (close-low) targets a support-recovery signal instead of raw range, and stays distinct from the other range-family mutation in this batch.

Raw $volume is not comparable across large-cap price levels; every other volume-based expression in this set uses $dollar_volume instead. That inconsistency is the weakest component here; swapping it in fixes cross-sectional comparability without touching the correlation structure.

$leverage has an ambiguous sign versus forward returns (can reflect either risk or efficient capital use), making it the likely weak leg. Swapping to $accrual_gap turns this into a quality-minus-accruals composite with a more robust expected sign, one leaf changed, quality term untouched.

Rule 11 already found rank-wrapping this factor unhelpful. A raw 21-day average dollar volume is just a slow-moving size proxy with little timing signal; swapping the aggregator to TS_STD targets liquidity instability instead of level, a single operator change.

Rule 8 shows same-field momentum is the weak leg that only survives fused with a fundamental; rule 4's other acceptance used a decay-weighted return, not a flat sum. Replacing TS_SUM with TS_DECAY_LINEAR upgrades that identified weak leg while preserving the validated return x fundamental-zscore structure untouched.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Each parent is shown with its fitness and nothing else. Fitness is a single scalar in which higher is better; it already accounts for significance, year-to-year stability, complexity and turnover. You are not given per-year, coverage, turnover or horizon diagnostics in this run, so choose the component to change from the expression itself.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. The 21-day close-position-in-high/low-range family (($close-TS_MIN($low,21))/(TS_MAX($high,21)-TS_MIN($low,21))) is saturated and load-bearing: a 5-day variant hit 0.898 correlation, a close-mean variant shared 9 archive nodes, and a close-only simplification lost 56% of parent IC. Stop proposing near-variants or simplifications of it.
  2. TS_ARGMAX/TS_ARGMIN of price extremes failed twice this round at different gates (40-day: cheap_screen; 200-day: coverage) - no evidence yet that standalone extremum-timing adds value.
  3. SIGN($accrual_gap) as a multiplicative gate on summed return scored far worse (t=0.08) than any other rejection this round - treat it as actively destructive, not merely unhelpful.
  4. This round's only acceptance paired a short (3-day) decayed return with a fundamental z-score (operating_margin), not another price/return term - favor return x fundamental-zscore pairings over return x price-extreme or return x return-vol.
  5. RANK or ZSCORE of a single fundamental leaf (e.g. RANK($roa)) is too shallow to ever pass crossover_not_a_fusion as a whole-tree parent, since the entire donor is just that one small fragment. Caused 5 of this round's rejections, all pairing RANK($roa) with a second subtree. Embed such leaves in a larger expression before using them as a crossover parent.
  6. The high-low range normalized by $open or $dollar_volume motif is over-mined: three crosses/window-variants of this same pair were all rejected this round for overlapping an existing archive member. Rest this family for a few rounds.
  7. Cosmetic re-wraps of archived winners (adding CS_DEMEAN, nudging a window slightly, or swapping CS_RANK for CS_ZSCORE) keep failing for overlapping the parent too closely, three times this round, including two variants of the best-performing overnight-gap factor. Extend winners with new fields or real sub-expressions, not outer wrapper changes.
  8. Same-field price momentum (return-sum differences, price-to-own-MA ratios, new-high counts) failed the cheap screen standalone across every window tried this round, 5 to 120 days. The same return-sum idea passed once fused from the start with a zscored fundamental (asset_turnover). Pair weak momentum candidates with a fundamental at proposal time rather than screening them standalone.
  9. This round's best factor is a cross-field ratio of open to prior close, not a same-field trailing-return construct. Favor overnight or cross-field price relationships over same-asset momentum ratios and sums.
  10. A bare rank of a single fundamental's raw multi-month delta, with no price or volume interaction, also failed the cheap screen this round. Fundamentals need a richer transform or an interaction partner, not just rank-of-delta.
  11. Reordering RANK and TS_MEAN around $dollar_volume, rank then smooth vs. smooth then rank, produced a near-duplicate of the plain smoothed version already known. Not a source of novelty for slow-moving, cross-sectionally stable fields.
  12. In the close-position-in-range family, the denominator's ceiling term must stay $high, not $close; swapping it in this round destroyed most of the parent's IC. Preserve the $high and $low pairing when varying or simplifying this family.

Return exactly one mutation per parent, 10 in total.
